belgium/grand-place.name: Grand-Place, Brussels
belgium/grand-place.description: The gilded guildhall square at the heart of Brussels, a UNESCO site.
belgium/grand-place.details: The Grand-Place is ringed by ornate guildhalls and the Gothic town hall, and is lit up at night. Biennial flower carpets cover it in August in some years. The surrounding lanes hold chocolate shops, waffle stands and beer bars, and nearby is the Manneken Pis. It is best early morning or after dark.

belgium/brussels-museums.name: Magritte Museum and comic-strip walls
belgium/brussels-museums.description: Surrealist art and Belgian comic heritage in the capital.
belgium/brussels-museums.details: The Magritte Museum holds the largest collection of the surrealist painter work. Brussels is also the home of the comic strip, with murals of Tintin, the Smurfs and Lucky Luke on walls around the centre and a Comic Strip Museum. Allow half a day for either.

belgium/atomium.name: Atomium
belgium/atomium.description: The giant atom-shaped building from the 1958 World Expo, with views from the top sphere.
belgium/atomium.details: The Atomium is a stainless steel model of an iron crystal, with spheres linked by tubes and escalators. The top sphere has a panorama of Brussels. Exhibitions fill the other spheres. It is on the northern edge of the city, reached by metro.

belgium/chocolate-beer.name: Belgian chocolate and beer tasting
belgium/chocolate-beer.description: A walking tasting of pralines, waffles and Belgian beers in the old centre.
belgium/chocolate-beer.details: Brussels is full of chocolatiers and bars with long beer lists. A guided tasting walk or a small brewery visit, such as the Cantillon lambic brewery, links the history to what you taste. Beers can be strong, so pace yourself.

belgium/bruges-belfry.name: Bruges Markt and Belfry
belgium/bruges-belfry.description: The medieval market square with a 83-metre belfry that visitors can climb.
belgium/bruges-belfry.details: The Belfry of Bruges has 366 steps to a view over the red roofs, and a carillon that rings on the hour. The Markt below is lined with step-gabled houses and horse carriages. Climb early, because tickets are timed. It is next to the Burg square and the Basilica of the Holy Blood.

belgium/bruges-canal-boat.name: Bruges canal boat tour
belgium/bruges-canal-boat.description: A thirty-minute boat ride along the medieval waterways, passing bridges and gardens.
belgium/bruges-canal-boat.details: Small open boats leave from several jetties around the centre, with guides in several languages. The ride passes the Rozenhoedkaai, one of the most photographed views in the city. Queues are shortest in the morning or the evening. Bring a layer in cool weather.

belgium/begijnhof.name: Begijnhof and Minnewater
belgium/begijnhof.description: A peaceful walled almshouse court and the Lake of Love on the south side of Bruges.
belgium/begijnhof.details: The Begijnhof is a tranquil enclosure of whitewashed houses around a lawn that blooms with daffodils in spring. Minnewater park has a lake with swans and a lock house. Together they offer a quiet respite from the busy centre, a short walk from the train station.

belgium/bruges-beer-brewery.name: De Halve Maan brewery
belgium/bruges-beer-brewery.description: The last working brewery in the centre of Bruges, with tours and a rooftop terrace.
belgium/bruges-beer-brewery.details: De Halve Maan has been brewing in the heart of Bruges for generations and makes the Brugse Zot and Straffe Hendrik beers. Tours show the brewery, finishing with a beer on the roof terrace. Tickets are timed and sell out in summer.

belgium/ghent-gravensteen.name: Gravensteen castle, Ghent
belgium/ghent-gravensteen.description: A moated medieval castle of the Counts of Flanders in the middle of the city.
belgium/ghent-gravensteen.details: Gravensteen has towers, a keep, dungeons and a collection of medieval weapons, with views over Ghent from the walls. An audio guide tells the story with some humour. It is on the edge of the old centre near the Graslei.

belgium/ghent-altarpiece.name: St Bavo Cathedral and the Ghent Altarpiece
belgium/ghent-altarpiece.description: The medieval cathedral that houses the Van Eyck masterpiece Adoration of the Mystic Lamb.
belgium/ghent-altarpiece.details: The Ghent Altarpiece, completed in 1432, is one of the most important paintings in Europe and is displayed in a dedicated area of the cathedral after a long restoration. Timed tickets are needed. Allow an hour for the visit with the audio guide.

belgium/graslei-korenlei.name: Graslei and Korenlei
belgium/graslei-korenlei.description: The two quays along the Leie that are the most photogenic spot in Ghent.
belgium/graslei-korenlei.details: The guild houses along the Graslei and Korenlei date from the Middle Ages and look best at dusk when lit. Terraces and boat tours line the canal. Ghent is livelier and less crowded than Bruges, with a large student population.

belgium/antwerp-cathedral.name: Cathedral of Our Lady and Rubens
belgium/antwerp-cathedral.description: Belgium largest Gothic cathedral, with paintings by Rubens inside.
belgium/antwerp-cathedral.details: The cathedral in Antwerp has a tall spire visible across the city and four paintings by Rubens, including The Descent from the Cross. The Grote Markt sits next to it, with guildhalls and the town hall. The Rubenshuis, the artist home, is a short walk away.

belgium/antwerp-diamond-fashion.name: Antwerp diamond district and fashion
belgium/antwerp-diamond-fashion.description: The world centre of the diamond trade, plus the stylish shops of the fashion quarter.
belgium/antwerp-diamond-fashion.details: Antwerp handles most of the world rough diamonds, and the DIVA museum tells the story. The Nationalestraat and surrounding streets are the heart of its fashion scene. Central Station is a showpiece of train architecture and worth a look.

belgium/ypres-flanders-fields.name: Ypres and Flanders Fields
belgium/ypres-flanders-fields.description: A rebuilt town and battlefield memorials from the First World War, including the Menin Gate.
belgium/ypres-flanders-fields.details: Ypres was destroyed in 1914 to 1918 and rebuilt. The In Flanders Fields Museum in the Cloth Hall tells the story, and the Menin Gate holds a nightly Last Post ceremony at 8pm. Nearby are the Tyne Cot cemetery and Passchendaele museum. It is a moving day, best with a guide.

belgium/ostend-coast.name: Ostend and the Belgian coast tram
belgium/ostend-coast.description: A seaside town on the North Sea, with a long beach and a coastal tram.
belgium/ostend-coast.details: The Kusttram runs the length of the Belgian coast, and Ostend has a promenade, seafood restaurants and the Mercator sailing ship. It is easy to reach by train from Bruges or Ghent. The water is cold, and the wind off the sea is strong.
